gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a 3-in-1 Qi2 25W stand draws more than the 30W adapter Apple names for its puck (25 W phone + 5 W Watch + 5 W AirPods = 35 W of output, so ESR ships a 50W wall charger), or that the car end also needs at least 35 W, which rules out a car's built-in USB port; the ESR 3-in-1 + OmniLock bundle comes with both adapters, a 50W wall charger and a 40W USB-C car adapter.
standout_why: I compared against Apple Support 105047 (cited in both home-and-car chats), Macworld's best-MagSafe-chargers page, Anker's MagSafe car-mount guide, the Anker A2933 page and the Apple puck pages. Apple Support only covers the single puck: 30W gets 25 W, 20W gets 15 W. ChatGPT turned that into '30W or higher' and applied it to the whole home setup. Macworld's roundup lists an included 30W or 45W charger for two Belkin 2-in-1s only and gives no wattage for a 3-in-1 and nothing on car input. Anker's guide (shown in the first home-and-car chat's results but not cited) does say to use 45W+ input in the car and not the car's built-in USB-C port, so the car half is partly covered. Neither half is stated anywhere as a sum: no page adds up the home stand's output, and none points out that both ends of the kit need a source of at least 35 W.
kit_items: Home 3-in-1 stand: ESR CryoBoost 3-in-1 Magnetic Charging Station (25W, Qi2.2). It charges the phone at 25 W and the Watch and AirPods at 5 W each, 35 W in total. Macworld says it ships with a 50W USB-C wall charger, so no 30W adapter needs to be bought.

Car mount: ESR OmniLock Magnetic Car Charger (25W, CryoBoost, Air Vent). 9to5Mac says it needs at least 35 W input for Qi2.2 speed and ships with a 12V adapter whose USB-C port gives 40 W. The car's own USB port is unlikely to be enough. The clip fits vent blades 10–32 mm wide and 1–4 mm thick; it does not fit round or bladeless vents.

Phone check (no purchase): the full 25 W only reaches iPhone 17, 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max, 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, 16 Plus and 16 Pro Max. iPhone 16 and 16 Pro get 22.5 W, iPhone Air 20 W, and iPhone 17e or iPhone 15 and older 15 W (Apple's own puck figures).
